Subject: Solaris Systems — partner assembly & interop readiness

Hi Elena / Tom,

Great to meet you both last week. Following up to kick off the technical validation for the Solaris + Redwood connector we discussed. Primary goal: get a smoke POC running in your staging environment and validate reference architecture expectations (latency, throughput, fallbacks).

Proposed agenda for the first technical session (60m):
- Quick intros (5m)
- Reference architecture walkthrough (10m) [attachment] 
- Network/topology & security requirements (10m)
- Test plan overview and success criteria (15m)
- Next steps / timeline / owners (20m)

Attachments: solaris_ref_arch_v1.png (reference design) — see diagram for recommended VPC peering and optional private control-plane flow.

Can you share 2x 1-hour slots next week when your infra + security folks can join? Also confirm whether you prefer a Hosted POC (fast) or Dedicated/Private POC (we can spin a private stack but needs lead time).

I'll loop in Lauren for test plan and Sergio for credentials/runbook.

Thanks,
Markus
Director, Partner Engineering
Redwood Inference

- Tue 2026-11-09 09:00-11:00 PT
- Wed 2026-11-10 13:00-15:00 PT

A couple of clarifying questions before the session so our security lead can prep:
1) For the reference architecture you sent, is the private control-plane option compatible with our strict egress policy (no public outbound except to specific FQDNs)?
2) Do you support mutual TLS for the agent-to-control-plane channel and client cert pinning?
3) Can you confirm which model variants you recommend for a latency-sensitive text-generation workload vs a batch-embedding workload — we want to pre-select workloads for the POC.

CC'd Kai from Edge Consulting — they will help orchestrate the POC on our side.

Regards,
Elena Vargas
Head of Integrations, Solaris Systems
elena.vargas@solaris-systems.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Solaris Systems — partner assembly & interop readiness

Hi Elena — thanks, and helpful questions. Short answers up front then we'll cover in the session: 
- Private control-plane: yes, compatible with strict egress. We document a minimal allowed FQDN/IP set and can whitelist just our control-plane endpoints.
- mTLS & cert pinning: supported. We provide instructions for mutual TLS configuration and recommended cert rotation cadence.
- Model variants: for low-latency generation we recommend a quantized 7B variant with AVX/opt kernels (or a trimmed 13B if you need higher quality). For embeddings/batch workloads the 2-3B optimized embedding model is typically best cost/throughput.

I've attached an initial test-plan draft (solaris_test_plan_v0.3.docx) with suggested success criteria and sample prompts. Please review and flag anything you want added.

Key ask for POC prep:
- Confirm expected concurrent requests and average sequence lengths for generation (tokens).
- If you choose Private POC, list the team that will own certs/firewalls.

Thanks — happy to walk through this on Tue/Wed.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: solaris_test_plan_v0.3.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

Date: 2026-11-04T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Solaris Systems — partner assembly & interop readiness

Hi Lauren / Markus,

Thanks — some details on our side to seed the test plan:
- Expected steady-state: ~45 concurrent generation requests across 3 services, peak bursts to 140 concurrent for short intervals.
- Typical generation size: 60-160 tokens (mostly prompts + short completions).
- Embedding batch jobs: nightly job that sends ~1.5M texts in 6-hour windows.

We are leaning toward starting with Hosted POC (faster), then if performance/cost checks out evaluate a Dedicated pool. One question: what quantization levels do you recommend for production cost reduction while retaining quality in generation? Are there recommended fallback model variants if the quantized variant underperforms?

Also can Redwood create a short-lived dedicated POC token/credentials we can use in staging? That will let our infra team run load scripts ahead of the call.

Tom Barlow
Senior Engineering Manager, Solaris Systems
Tom.Barlow@solaris-systems.com

Elena / Tom — thanks all, summary & next steps: 

POC kickoff session: 2026-11-10 14:00 PT (confirmed) — we will run through the ref-arch, security checklist, and the test-plan scenarios.

Action items:
- Sergio: send scoped POC token + api_credentials_readme.txt to security@solaris-systems.com (in progress).
- Lauren: lead the architecture walkthrough and finalize test-plan (update v0.4 with Solaris numbers).
- Solaris (Tom): run dry load with the provided token before the call and share initial latency/5xx metrics.
- Kai (Edge Consulting): manage orchestration on Solaris side and gather any infra blockers.

Success criteria (for the POC):
- Average p95 latency < 220ms for 60–160 token generation under 45 concurrent steady-state
- Embedding nightly batch completes within the 6-hour window without >1% job failure rate
- No critical security findings for hosted control-plane connectivity (or a documented mitigation plan)

If these look good we'll use the session to validate and decide whether to continue to a Dedicated pool evaluation. I'll share the meeting invite with dial-in shortly.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — see you on the call.

-Markus
Director, Partner Engineering
Redwood Inference
